messages:
Eleni (Finance): Heads up: vendor 'DresdenML GmbH' invoiced Redwood Inference EU for services (model tuning) and charged 19% German VAT. Invoice VAT ID shown: DE123456789. They flagged they only invoice DE VAT by default.

Maya (Finance): Do we have an EU company entity on record for this vendor? We should be on a B2B reverse-charge (0%) if our invoice is to Redwood Inference Ireland Ltd (IE) and we have a valid VAT number.

Eleni (Finance): Bill-to on the invoice is "Redwood Inference Ireland Ltd" with VAT IE9876543V. Vendor attached PDF but no VIES lookup proof.

Sergio (Tax EMEA): Quick checklist: 1) confirm buyer VAT (IE9876543V) is valid via VIES; 2) vendor VAT (DE123456789) should be valid and the invoice should include a reverse-charge statement (ie "VAT reverse-charged under Article 196 TFEU" or local language equivalent); 3) invoice must show both VAT numbers and the line "VAT 0% - reverse charge" or similar.

Jon (AP): If VAT is charged incorrectly we either ask vendor to re-issue without VAT or we accept and reclaim through local VAT reclaim (painful). Reissue preferred. For payment timing, shall we pause until vendor corrects?

Maya (Finance): Hold payment until vendor replies but don't exceed contract SLA. Ask vendor to reissue an invoice zero-rated under reverse charge and include both VAT IDs and the statutory text.

Eleni (Finance): Drafting message to vendor now 12:```
Hi DresdenML team,

Thanks for the invoice. Our AP team has flagged VAT charged at 19% but the supply is cross-border B2B within the EU. To process payment we need either:

A) A corrected invoice that zero-rates VAT under the EU reverse-charge mechanism showing: both VAT numbers (your DE number and our buyer VAT IE9876543V), the statement that VAT is reverse-charged (e.g., "VAT reverse-charged under Article 196 TFEU"), and VAT line showing 0% or no VAT charged; OR

B) If you believe German VAT is due, please provide the legal basis and confirm why reverse-charge does not apply.

Please also provide a copy/screenshot of your VIES VAT validation (https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/) for DE123456789 and confirm the buyer VAT displayed there matches IE9876543V.

If we don't receive a corrected invoice we may need to withhold payment while we sort VAT treatment which could delay payment.

Thanks,
Eleni (Finance)
```

Jon (AP): Add: 'Please include the registered legal name that matches your German Handelsregister entry' so our AP system matches vendor record.

Sergio (Tax EMEA): Add: 'For automation: include the VIES response screenshot or VIES reference number (timestamped) to speed validation.'

Eleni (Finance): Sent. Vendor replied: "We are a small DE supplier and always add VAT by default. We don't have experience with reverse-charge. We can re-issue if you confirm that's correct. Our VAT ID is valid."

Maya (Finance): Great 12 — ask them to re-issue. Also attach the reissued PDF to vendor record when received and flag vendor onboarding to request VAT status upfront for EU suppliers.

Jon (AP): I'll hold the invoice in AP queue, set currency = EUR, and wait for corrected invoice. If they re-issue with reverse charge, I will code VAT = 0 and proceed.

Sergio (Tax EMEA): If they reissue correctly we don't owe VAT. If they persist in charging DE VAT and we pay, we can file a reclaim through German tax portal possibly but that's more admin. Reissue is the clean route.

Eleni (Finance): Thanks all. Noting follow-up: add VAT validation step to vendor onboarding checklist, and ask Sales to include buyer VAT on SOWs for EU contracts. Closing this thread after vendor re-issue. :white_check_mark:
